C.a: T1- Every ten years the census counts how many people live in each state. E2- If a state gains or loses people it can gain or lose House seats, like Texas gained two after 2020. A3- So the lines have to be redrawn so each district has about the same population.

F.a: T1- An independent commission could draw the lines instead of politicians. E2- States like California use citizen commissions. A3- Since the commission doesn't care which party wins, they won't split up Party B on purpose.

A compactness requirement means districts have to be neat shapes, not weird ones. Plan 2's districts are long slices that cut up Party B's area, so a compact rule would keep Party B's cluster together and they'd win some seats.
If a nonpartisan commission made the maps, the people in power couldn't draw lines to help themselves stay in power.
Compactness rules ban strange-shaped districts, which makes it harder to crack a group of voters apart.
